title: Sort by length, break ties, and keep the nulls in their place

blocks.text: `sorted()` uses natural order and throws `NullPointerException` on a `null` element; `sorted(Comparator)` sorts by any rule, and comparators compose: `Comparator.comparingInt(...).thenComparing(...)` breaks ties, and `Comparator.nullsFirst(Comparator.naturalOrder())` places `null` before everything else.

items: `byLengthThenAlpha(List<String> words)` sorts the words by length, shortest first, and words of equal length alphabetically.
`nullsFirst(List<String> names)` sorts the names in natural order, with every `null` before them.

blocks.text: A sort by length alone keeps equal-length words in the order they came in.

cases.says: It sorts words by length, and names in natural order.
Words of the same length are ordered alphabetically, with thenComparing.
Null names sort first instead of throwing: sorted() with natural order throws on null, Comparator.nullsFirst does not.

concepts: sorted(Comparator) sorts by any rule, and a null-safe comparator such as nullsFirst sorts nulls without throwing.
